samples.summary: The identical `""` → `undefined` reset fix in DocsFormattingToolbar has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes two reset call sites in `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx` (`onReset={() => handleTextColor(undefined)}` at ~line 490 and `handleHighlightColor(undefined)` at ~line 512), but the only new frontend test (`packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts`) renders `TextFormatGroup` only. I grepped the frontend tests for `applyStyle({ color`, `color: undefined`, `color: ""` and globbed `packages/frontend/tests/**/*docs*` — the docs toolbar tests present are `docs-context-menu.test.tsx` and `docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx`, neither of which touches the color picker. So the second (docs-specific, and the one the issue is filed against) component can regress back to `""` with the suite still green.
searchedFor: grep applyStyle\(\{ color / color: undefined / color: "" in packages/frontend

samples.summary: `expect(fills).not.toContain(`hi:${SELECTION_FILL}`)` cannot fail — the stub records assignments verbatim and never inherits
samples.evidence: The stub's `set fillStyle(v) { fillStyle = v }` accepts any string, so the pre-fix code path would record `hi:` (empty string), never `hi:rgba(1, 2, 3, 0.5)`. The documented failure mode (a real canvas IGNORING an invalid assignment and keeping the previous fill) is not reproduced by the stub, so the SELECTION_FILL preset and this negative assertion are decoration; only the sibling `toContain(`hi:${Theme.defaultColor}`)` does real work. Same pattern in `paint-layout.test.ts` (`makeFillStyleCtx(Theme.selectionColor)`) and `render-list-marker.test.ts` lines 110/118 where `ctx.fillStyle = PREVIOUS_FILL` is dead setup with a comment claiming it "reproduces that inheritance".

samples.summary: `isTransparentAlpha`'s documented "unparseable alpha ⇒ opaque" rule is untested
samples.evidence: The helper explicitly promises that an alpha it cannot parse is treated as opaque so a visible color is never dropped, but the new tests in `packages/docs/test/model/color.test.ts` and `test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts` only cover `0`, `0%` and `0.5`. Nothing exercises e.g. `rgba(1, 2, 3, none)` / `rgba(1,2,3,)` (which would silently start dropping colors if the branch inverted), nor the `Number.isNaN` channel guard (`rgb(., 0, 0)`), nor the whitespace-trim path (`' #ff0000 '`).

samples.summary: `not.toContain('a"/><w:b')` asserts against escaping the exporter never applies
samples.evidence: The cell-fill path only ever interpolates or drops the value; no XML-attribute escaping exists on this sink, so the escaped form could never appear and the assertion holds regardless of behavior. Same for the redundant `not.toContain('w:fill="a"/>')` in `docx-style-map.test.ts` after `not.toContain('<w:shd')`. Harmless, since the count assertion (`docXml.match(/<w:shd /g)!.length === 2`) is the one that carries the test.

samples.summary: `toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` also passes for `applyStyle({})`, so it can't assert the "explicit undefined key" claim in the comment
samples.evidence: Vitest's argument equality uses toEqual semantics, which ignore keys whose value is `undefined`; the test therefore cannot distinguish `{ color: undefined }` (attribute removal, what the comment says matters) from `{}`. It does still catch the `''` regression, so the coverage is real but weaker than advertised — `expect('color' in call[0]).toBe(true)` or `toStrictEqual` would close the gap.
